title: The Fee Proposal Leaves the Stage, but Oil Worries Stay On
part1:
Onstage, the lead role changed hands. But the audience’s worries stayed the same. This time, the crude oil market unfolded like a play.

It began with an announcement by Mr. Trump. He said that all goods passing through the Strait of Hormuz would face a 20 percent fee to cover the cost of keeping the strait safe. Crude oil futures prices rose sharply that day. But the fee proposal was not the only reason for the rise. There were also worries about the sea blockade against Iran, which was due to begin the next day, and whether ships carrying energy could pass safely.
part2: The next day, Mr. Trump withdrew the fee proposal, citing “very productive talks” with leaders in the Middle East. Instead, he announced deals on trade with the United States and investment with Gulf countries. The idea of charging a fee on goods passing through the strait was replaced by plans to move ahead with deals with the United States. Based on the headlines alone, it might look as if the matter was settled.
part3:
After the announcement, crude oil futures prices gave back some of their gains for a while. But they soon returned to a high level close to where they had been before the announcement. Even though the fee proposal, one of the play’s characters, left the stage, worries remained about the sea blockade, attacks between the United States and Iran, and the safety of tankers.

The market was not looking only at whether there would be a fee. Could ships travel safely? Would the oil arrive? Until those questions had clear answers, worry would not leave the stage, even after the announcement was withdrawn.

In other words, the news story can change in a day, but conditions at sea do not change in a day. Perhaps the crude oil market was watching a story that would keep going.
in_one_line: Trump withdrew the proposed Strait of Hormuz fee, but oil markets remained worried about shipping safety and supply.
